buxton_well_0.text: St Ann's Well. The water comes out at about 28 degrees all year round. Mild as a Tuesday.
The Romans knew this place as Aquae Arnemetiae, the waters of the goddess Arnemetia. Not an easy name for an address.
The rain falls on the hills, sinks deep, warms in the rock and rises here years later. Slow travel, but worth the wait.

then.text: Another bottle? You will slosh. Off you go, and mind the hills.

else.text: Here, a bottle to take with you. It is good for the road, and for arguing with your sister.

then.text: Want to use the bottling table?

else.text: Spring water from the well, elderflower from the hedge, and a pinch of something I'm not allowed to tell you.
Fine, it's sugar. Mix them up and it clears whatever ails a creature. Better than Buxton Water. Don't tell my boss.
Pop in whenever you've got the makings. You can use my kitchen.
